items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「アジの三杯」は、瀬戸内海で夏から秋にとれる小アジを、酢と砂糖、しょうゆを合わせた三杯酢に漬けた郷土料理。焼き立てのアジを酢に漬けることで骨までやわらかくなり、頭から尾まで丸ごと食べられる。香ばしく焼けたアジの身と、爽やかな酸味の効いた三杯酢が合わさり、唐辛子やしょうが、みょうがなどの薬味がぴりっとした風味を添える。仕上げにすだちや青じそを添えることもあり、さっぱりとした後味の一品になっている。
## どう作るのか
アジは腹わたを取り除き、焦げ目がつくまで香ばしく焼く。酢、砂糖、しょうゆを合わせた三杯酢に、唐辛子や刻みしょうが、せん切りのみょうがなどの薬味を加え、焼きたてのアジを漬け込む。冷めるまで漬けておくと骨までやわらかくなるため、粗熱が取れるまでじっくり時間をかけるのがコツとされる。仕上げにすだちや青じそを添えて供する。アジのほかサッパやキスなど、その時々にとれる小魚でも同じように作られるという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
瀬戸内海は浅瀬が多くプランクトンが豊富なことから、アジをはじめとした魚介に恵まれた海域とされる。夏から秋に入ってくる小アジを、酢に漬けることで骨まで食べられるようにし、日持ちもさせる工夫が三杯酢仕立てにつながったと考えられる。かつては地引き網の手伝いをすると漁師から魚を分けてもらう習わしがあったといい、身近な魚を余さず味わう暮らしの知恵が根底にあるようだ。夏祭りの酒の肴としても親しまれてきたという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Aji no sanbai marinates small horse mackerel, caught in the Seto Inland Sea from summer into autumn, in a "sanbaizu" sauce made of vinegar, sugar, and soy sauce. Marinating the freshly grilled fish in the vinegar softens even the bones, so the whole fish, head to tail, can be eaten. The smoky flavor of the grilled mackerel meets the bright tang of the vinegar, with chili, ginger, and myoga ginger adding a sharp kick. Sudachi citrus or shiso leaves are sometimes added for a clean finish.
## How it's made
The mackerel is gutted and grilled until lightly charred. Vinegar, sugar, and soy sauce are combined into a sanbaizu sauce, seasoned with chili, chopped ginger, and julienned myoga, and the freshly grilled fish is marinated in it. Leaving it to marinate until it cools is said to be the key to softening the bones fully, so cooks take their time rather than rushing the soak. It's served with sudachi or shiso to taste. Besides horse mackerel, other small fish caught at the time, such as sappa or Japanese whiting, are said to be used the same way.
## Why it took this shape
The Seto Inland Sea is shallow and rich in plankton, conditions said to make it abundant in fish including horse mackerel. Marinating the summer and autumn catch in vinegar so the bones could be eaten and the fish would keep longer appears to be what led to the sanbaizu treatment. Fishermen reportedly used to share their catch with anyone who helped haul the beach seine nets, and the dish seems to reflect a practical habit of making full use of fish that were close at hand. It's also said to have long been enjoyed as a drinking snack at summer festivals.

sources.title: アジの三杯 うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
白みそ仕立ての汁に、あんこ入りの丸餅と輪切りの大根、金時にんじんなどを入れた雑煮。白みその甘みとコクに、餅の中からとろりと出るあんの甘さが重なり、ほかの地域の雑煮とは一線を画す濃厚な甘みが特徴とされる。白みそは大豆を控えめに米麹を多く使い、塩分を抑えて仕込んだ甘口のみそで、12月ごろに仕込んで正月に合わせて1カ月ほど熟成させるという。仕上げに青のりを振りかけ、彩りよく盛り付ける。
## どう作るのか
煮干しでとっただし汁に、丸く輪切りにした大根と金時にんじんを入れて柔らかく煮る。あん入りの丸餅を加えて柔らかくなったら豆腐を入れ、ひと煮立ちさせてから煮汁で溶いた白みそを加える。椀の底に大根を敷いて餅がくっつかないようにし、その上に餅、さらに大根とにんじんを彩りよく盛り付け、青のりを振って仕上げる。里芋や白ねぎを加える家庭もあるという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
温暖で雨の少ない香川ではかつてさとうきび栽培が奨励され、讃岐地方の白砂糖は特産品の一つになったとされる。砂糖が貴重だった時代、年に一度、正月にとっておきの砂糖を使ってあん餅を作り雑煮に入れたことが始まりと伝わる。一方の白みそは、保元の乱で讃岐に流された崇徳上皇のもとへ京都から伝わったとされ、冬場の調味料として重宝されてきたという。二つの貴重な甘味と旨みが正月という特別な日に組み合わさったことが、この雑煮の形につながったと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Anmochi zōni is a New Year's soup with a white miso base, filled with round rice cakes stuffed with sweet bean paste, along with sliced daikon and Kintoki carrot. The sweetness and richness of the white miso meet the oozing sweetness of the bean paste inside the rice cake, giving it a richer sweetness than zōni found elsewhere. The white miso itself is a mild, sweet variety made with less soybean and more rice malt, low in salt, typically prepared in December and left to age about a month before New Year's. The dish is finished with a sprinkle of green nori for color.
## How it's made
Dashi made from dried sardines is used to simmer round-cut daikon and Kintoki carrot until tender. The bean-paste-filled rice cakes are added and cooked until soft, then tofu goes in, and once it comes back to a boil, white miso thinned with some of the broth is stirred in. Daikon is laid at the bottom of the bowl so the rice cake does not stick, topped with the rice cake, then more daikon and carrot arranged for color, finished with a scattering of green nori. Some households add taro or leeks as well.
## Why it took this shape
Kagawa's mild, dry climate once encouraged sugarcane cultivation, and Sanuki's white sugar is said to have become one of the region's signature products. In an age when sugar was precious, making bean-paste rice cakes with a once-a-year allotment of good sugar for New Year's is said to be how this dish began. The white miso, meanwhile, is said to have been brought from Kyoto by people traveling to and from Emperor Sutoku, exiled to Sanuki after the Hōgen Rebellion, and it became a valued winter seasoning. Combining these two precious sweet, savory ingredients for the special occasion of New Year's appears to be what shaped this zōni.

sources.title: あんもち雑煮 うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
酢飯に季節の野菜や魚介を混ぜ合わせたちらしずし。客をもてなす際には、サワラやサバ、コノシロを酢でしめたものやアナゴの照り焼き、錦糸卵、紅しょうが、木の芽などを彩りよく盛りつける。酢飯の酸味と旬の具材の風味が重なり、祭りや祝い事にふさわしい華やかな味わいになる。中讃地域の宇多津町では甘めの味付けが特徴とされ、地域によって味付けの濃淡が異なるという。
## どう作るのか
昆布と酒を合わせて米を炊き、エビはゆで、里芋やごぼうなどの具材は薄味に煮ておく。合わせ酢を混ぜたご飯に具材を加えて手早くかき混ぜ、器に盛り付ける。仕上げにアナゴの照り焼きや錦糸卵を彩りよくのせる。使う具材は季節や家庭によってさまざまで、旬の魚介や野菜を取り入れて作られるという。手早く混ぜてご飯粒をつぶさないようにするのが、口当たりよく仕上げるコツとされる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
ばらずしは神社の祭りや節句、棟上げ、結婚披露宴、法事など、地域の行事のたびに振る舞われるごちそうだったとされる。宇多津町は江戸時代に高松藩の港として栄え、砂糖を入手しやすい土地柄だったとされるほか、塩づくりが盛んな地域では体力を使う仕事に従事する人々に甘い味付けが好まれたとも伝わる。人が集まる場でその時々の旬の具材を持ち寄って作ることが、地域の歴史や文化を伝える機会にもなってきたようだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Barazushi is a scattered sushi made by mixing seasonal vegetables and seafood into vinegared rice. For guests, it's often dressed up with mackerel, Spanish mackerel, or gizzard shad cured in vinegar, glazed conger eel, shredded egg crepe, red pickled ginger, and sansho leaf buds. The tang of the vinegared rice meets the flavor of seasonal ingredients for a dish festive enough for a celebration. In Utazu, in the Nakasan area, the seasoning is said to run sweeter than elsewhere, with the balance of flavor varying by region.
## How it's made
Rice is cooked with kelp and sake, shrimp is boiled, and ingredients like taro and burdock are lightly simmered. The seasoned rice is mixed with a vinegar blend and the prepared ingredients, tossed together quickly, and plated. It's finished with a colorful topping of glazed conger eel and shredded egg crepe. Mixing quickly without crushing the rice grains is said to be the trick to a pleasant texture. The ingredients used vary by season and household, drawing on whatever seafood and vegetables are in season.
## Why it took this shape
Barazushi is said to have been served as a festive dish at shrine festivals, seasonal celebrations, roof-raising ceremonies, wedding receptions, and memorial services. Utazu is said to have prospered as a port for the Takamatsu domain in the Edo period, giving it easier access to sugar, and in areas where salt production was a major local industry, sweeter seasoning is said to have been favored by workers doing physically demanding labor. Gathering to bring together whatever ingredients were in season appears to have made the dish a way of passing down local history and culture along with its flavor.

sources.title: ばらずし うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
どじょうをごぼうや里芋、長ねぎ、油揚げ、そして打ち込みうどんと一緒に煮込んだ汁物。どじょうは煮ると骨までやわらかくなり丸ごと食べられ、うなぎより脂肪分は少ないもののビタミンやミネラルを豊富に含むとされる。野菜の甘みとみそのコク、どじょうの滋味深い味わいが溶け合い、うどんが加わることで食べ応えのある一杯になる。中讃地域や東讃地域の一部で受け継がれてきた料理だという。
## どう作るのか
どじょうは水切りして酒に入れ、動きが止まったら塩でもんでぬめりを取る。鍋に水を入れて沸かし、切った油揚げ、里芋、なすを煮て、火が通ったら水洗いしたどじょうを加える。再び沸騰したらうどんを入れて軽く混ぜ、うどんが煮えたら残りの具材を合わせ、みそと酒で味を調える。どじょうを酒でしめてから塩もみすることで臭みが和らぐとされ、好みの薬味を添えて食べるという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
田植えが終わり農作業が一段落する土用のころ、男性がため池や川でどじょうをとってきて調理する風習があったとされる。暑さで体力を消耗しやすい時季に、栄養豊富などじょうと具だくさんの汁で夏バテを防ぐ料理として定着したと考えられる。集落の共同作業や寄り合いの際には大釜でまとめて炊き、近所や親戚に振る舞うことで親睦を深める役割も果たしてきたという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Dojō-jiru simmers loach together with burdock, taro, leek, fried tofu, and freshly made udon noodles. Boiling the loach softens even the bones so the whole fish can be eaten, and while it has less fat than eel, it's said to be rich in vitamins and minerals. The sweetness of the vegetables and the richness of the miso meet the loach's deep flavor, and the udon makes the dish substantial enough for a full meal. It's said to have been passed down mainly in the Nakasan area and parts of Tosan, in central and eastern Kagawa.
## How it's made
The loach is drained and placed in sake; once it stops moving, it's rubbed with salt to remove the slime. Water is boiled in a pot, and cut fried tofu, taro, and eggplant are simmered until cooked, then the rinsed loach is added. Once it returns to a boil, udon is added and lightly stirred in; once the noodles are cooked, the rest of the ingredients are added and the soup is seasoned with miso and sake. Stunning the loach in sake before salting it is said to soften its strong smell. It's served with condiments to taste.
## Why it took this shape
Around the "doyo" period, once rice planting had finished and farm work eased up, men are said to have gone out to catch loach from irrigation ponds and rivers. In the hot season when stamina runs low, this nutrient-rich fish simmered into a hearty, vegetable-packed soup appears to have taken hold as a way to fend off summer fatigue. At community work parties and village gatherings, it was reportedly cooked in a large communal pot and shared with neighbors and relatives, which also gave it a role in strengthening ties within the community.

sources.title: どじょう汁 うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
瀬戸内海でとれる体長10cmほどのシバエビを、頭も殻もむかずにすりつぶして仕立てた白みそ仕立ての汁物。エビの殻や頭から出る濃厚な風味とみその甘みが溶け合い、豆腐のやさしい食感が加わる。すりつぶした殻の食感がとろみとなって汁にほどよいコクを添えるのも特徴とされる。三豊市豊中町の宇賀神社で秋に開かれる「どぶろく祭り」で、ごはんやなますとともに振る舞われてきた郷土料理とされる。
## どう作るのか
米のとぎ汁を用意し、頭と尾を取ったエビを殻ごと塩水で洗ってボウルに入れ、とぎ汁を加えてミキサーにかける。残りのとぎ汁を鍋に入れて火にかけ、すりつぶしたエビを加えて混ぜながら煮立たせる。白みそを溶き入れて弱火で20分ほど煮たら、さいの目に切った豆腐を加えてさらに煮込み、焦げないよう混ぜながら仕上げる。器に盛り、仕上げにねぎを散らす。
## なぜこの形になったのか
豊中町の宇賀神社では、五穀豊穣への感謝を込めた秋祭りが古くから続けられてきたとされ、その際に神前に供えた後、参加者にどぶろくとともにえびみそ汁が振る舞われてきたという。瀬戸内海で身近にとれる小エビを、殻ごとすりつぶして無駄なく使う調理法が、祭りのごちそうとして定着した理由のひとつと考えられる。とぎ汁を活用する点も、身近にある材料を無駄にしない暮らしの知恵の表れといえそうだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
This white-miso soup is made from shiba shrimp, about ten centimeters long, caught in the Seto Inland Sea and blended whole, shell and head included. The concentrated flavor released from the shell and head melds with the sweetness of the miso, and cubes of tofu add a gentle texture. The ground shell also lends the broth a bit of body, giving the soup a pleasant richness. It's a dish said to have been served alongside rice and namasu at the autumn "doburo matsuri" festival held at Uga Shrine in Toyonaka, part of Mitoyo city.
## How it's made
Rice-rinsing water is set aside. The shrimp are headed and tailed, washed in salt water, and blended shell-on in a bowl with some of the rinsing water. The rest of the rinsing water goes into a pot and is brought to a boil, the blended shrimp is added and stirred as it comes back to a boil, then white miso is stirred in and simmered over low heat for about twenty minutes. Cubed tofu is added and simmered further, stirred carefully so it doesn't scorch, then served in a bowl topped with scallions.
## Why it took this shape
Uga Shrine in Toyonaka is said to have held an autumn festival giving thanks for the harvest for a long time, and after offerings were made at the shrine, ebi-miso-shiru was reportedly served to participants along with the festival's home-brewed sake. Grinding up small, locally caught shrimp shell and all so nothing goes to waste appears to be one reason the method became the way this festival dish was prepared. Using the rice-rinsing water, too, looks like another sign of a household habit of not letting anything close at hand go to waste.

sources.title: えびみそ汁 うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
小麦粉を水で練った生地をゆでただんごに、小豆やささげで作った甘いあんをまぶした素朴な菓子。収穫したばかりの新麦で作るだんごはつるりとした光沢があり、香りの良さが際立つという。あんをまぶした表面がまだらになる様子や、半夏生の頃に作ることから「はげ団子」と呼ばれるようになったとされる。地域によっては生地であんを包んで鉄板で焼いたり、蒸したりと仕上げ方もさまざまだという。
## どう作るのか
小豆やささげをたっぷりの水でやわらかく煮て、豆と同量の砂糖を加えてさらに煮詰め、塩をひとつまみ加えて甘みを引き立てる。小麦粉を水で練った生地を一口大にまとめ、沸かした湯に落として浮き上がってきたらざるに上げる。水気を切っただんごの全体にあんをまぶせば完成となる。地域によっては、あんの代わりにきな粉をまぶすこともあるという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
香川では麦を刈る5月から田植えの6月にかけて農繁期を迎え、7月2日ごろの半夏生を境に長雨が明け、農家は一区切りの休息をとるとされる。ちょうどそのころに収穫した新麦を使って団子を作り、神仏に供えてから家族で味わう習わしが根づいたと考えられる。農作業がひと段落する節目に、季節の恵みへの感謝を込めて食べる行事食として定着したようだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Hage-dango are dumplings made from wheat flour kneaded with water and boiled, then coated in a sweet paste of azuki or cowpea beans. Made with freshly harvested new wheat, the dumplings are said to have a glossy sheen and a distinctive aroma. The mottled look of the bean paste over the dumplings' surface, along with the timing of when they're made — around the seasonal marker hangeshō — is said to be behind the name "hage-dango." In some areas the paste is wrapped inside the dough and grilled on a griddle, or the dumplings are steamed instead, so the finish varies by region.
## How it's made
Azuki or cowpea beans are simmered in plenty of water until soft, then an equal amount of sugar is added and simmered further, with a pinch of salt said to bring out the sweetness. Wheat flour dough kneaded with water is shaped into bite-sized dumplings and dropped into boiling water; once they float, they're scooped out and drained. The drained dumplings are then coated all over in the bean paste to finish. In some areas roasted soybean flour is used in place of the paste.
## Why it took this shape
In Kagawa, the busy farming season runs from the wheat harvest in May through rice planting in June, and around July 2, the seasonal marker known as hangeshō, the long rains are said to end, giving farmers a chance to rest. Making dumplings from the newly harvested wheat around that time, offering them to the household gods and Buddha, and then sharing them as a family appears to be a custom that took root from that timing. It seems to have settled in as a seasonal dish eaten with gratitude for the harvest at a natural pause in farm work.

sources.title: はげ団子 うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
瀬戸内海でとれるタコと里芋を、しょうゆや砂糖などの調味料で煮付けたシンプルな一品。瀬戸内海のタコは貝類やエビ、カニなど栄養豊富なえさで育つため、身に甘みと強い風味があるとされる。里芋のほくほくとした食感とタコの弾力ある歯ごたえが調味だれと絡み合い、素朴ながら満足感のある味わいになる。タコにはたんぱく質やビタミン、タウリンがバランスよく含まれ、疲労回復にも良いとされてきたという。
## どう作るのか
タコは塩もみしてぬめりを取ってから、さっとゆでて食べやすい大きさに切る。里芋は小口に切り、塩でもんでぬめりを取っておく。鍋に調味料と切ったタコ、里芋を加え、味がしみ込むまで煮込めば完成となる。里芋にタコの旨みがしっかり染み込むまでじっくり煮るのがコツとされ、惣菜としてはもちろん、酒の肴として食卓に上がることも多いという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
里芋は親芋から次々と子芋が育つことから子孫繁栄の象徴とされ、正月や婚礼などハレの日のごちそうに用いられてきたと伝わる。田んぼの片隅で栽培されることも多く「田いも」とも呼ばれるほど身近な作物だったという。海の幸であるタコと里の幸である里芋を組み合わせたこの料理は、身近にある海と里の恵みを一皿にまとめた組み合わせとして根づいたと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Imotako simmers octopus and taro caught and grown around the Seto Inland Sea in soy sauce, sugar, and other seasonings — a simple dish. Octopus from the Seto Inland Sea feeds on nutrient-rich prey like shellfish, shrimp, and crab, and is said to develop a sweet, strongly flavored meat as a result. The mealy texture of the taro and the springy bite of the octopus soak up the seasoned broth together for a simple but satisfying dish. Octopus is said to offer a good balance of protein, vitamins, and taurine, and has long been valued as a food that helps with fatigue.
## How it's made
The octopus is rubbed with salt to remove its slime, briefly boiled, and cut into bite-sized pieces. The taro is cut into rounds and rubbed with salt to remove its own sliminess. Both go into a pot with seasoning and are simmered until the flavor soaks in. Letting it simmer long enough for the octopus's flavor to soak fully into the taro is said to be the key step. The dish is served both as an everyday side and as a snack with sake.
## Why it took this shape
Taro produces new corms from the parent plant year after year, and is said to have become a symbol of family prosperity as a result, valued as a festive dish for New Year's, weddings, and other special occasions. Often grown in a corner of the rice paddies, it's said to have been familiar enough to earn the nickname "paddy potato." Pairing octopus from the sea with taro from the fields appears to be a way this dish brought together the bounty close at hand from both land and sea.

sources.title: いもたこ うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
いりこ（煮干し）の頭と身の両方をだしと具に使う、西讃地域の炊き込みごはん。にんじん、大根、里芋、こんにゃくなどの具材とともに米を炊き込み、いりこの濃厚な旨みがご飯全体に行き渡る。瀬戸内海はカタクチイワシ漁が盛んで、獲れたてを短時間で加工することから、旨みの強いいりこが手に入りやすい土地柄とされる。いりこの身もほろりとした食感で、だしを取った後もそのまま食べられるのが特徴という。
## どう作るのか
いりこは頭と腹を取り除いて身を割り、頭は水につけてだしを取っておく。米、切った具材、いりこの身、いりこだし、調味料を釜に合わせて炊き上げる。きのこ類やごぼうを加える家庭も多く、具材は季節の野菜や好みによって少しずつ異なるという。いりこだしをしっかりと取ることが、うまみを引き出す決め手になるとされる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
瀬戸内海の穏やかな海で育つカタクチイワシは、いりこに加工すると濃厚で旨みの強いだしが取れるとされ、讃岐うどんをはじめ県内の家庭料理に欠かせない存在になっているという。いりこの身も無駄なくご飯に炊き込むいりこ飯は、良質ないりこが身近にあった土地ならではの、素材を余さず使い切る知恵から生まれた料理と考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Iriko-meshi is a rice dish from western Kagawa cooked with both the dashi and the meat of iriko, dried young sardines. Carrot, daikon, taro, and konjac are cooked into the rice along with it, and the deep flavor of the iriko spreads through every grain. The Seto Inland Sea supports a strong anchovy fishery, and because the catch is processed quickly after landing, the region is known for producing particularly flavorful iriko. The meat itself has a crumbly texture and is said to be eaten as is even after the dashi has been drawn from it.
## How it's made
The iriko are headed and split open, and the heads are soaked in water to make dashi. Rice, chopped vegetables, the iriko meat, the iriko dashi, and seasoning all go into the pot together to cook. Mushrooms or burdock are often added too, and the mix of vegetables varies with the season and the household's taste. Drawing a full-flavored dashi from the iriko is said to be the key to bringing out the dish's flavor.
## Why it took this shape
Anchovies raised in the calm waters of the Seto Inland Sea are said to yield a rich, deeply flavorful dashi once processed into iriko, and that dashi has become essential to home cooking across the prefecture, from Sanuki udon on down. Cooking the iriko meat directly into the rice as well, rather than discarding it after making dashi, looks like a way of making full use of a high-quality ingredient that was close at hand.

sources.title: いりこ飯 うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
たけのこやさやいんげん、にんじん、ごぼう、干ししいたけ、油揚げ、干しエビ、ちくわなど、海と山の幸をしょうゆなどで煮含め、炊きたてのご飯に混ぜ込んだ小豆島の郷土料理。「おまぜ」とも呼ばれ、具材それぞれの旨みが染み込んだ煮汁がご飯にほどよく絡み、彩り豊かで華やかな一皿になる。小豆島は醤油づくりが盛んな土地として知られ、地元のしょうゆで味付けすることも多いという。
## どう作るのか
米は通常どおりに炊き、干ししいたけと干しエビは水で戻す。ごぼうはささがきにし、さやいんげんは塩ゆでしてから斜めに切り、その他の具材も細かく切りそろえる。にんじんとさやいんげん以外の具材を鍋に入れ調味料とともに煮含め、味がしみたらにんじんとさやいんげんを加えてさらに煮る。炊いたご飯に具材と煮汁を混ぜ合わせて味を調え、器に盛れば完成となる。春はふきやさつまいもの茎、漁師町ではアナゴを加えるなど、季節や地域で具材が変わるという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
かきまぜは、親族や集落の集まり、農繁期に近所同士で助け合った際などハレの日に振る舞われてきたとされる。手早く調理できて大人数にも対応しやすく、見た目も華やかなことから、農村の女性たちに重宝されてきたと伝わる。海に囲まれた温暖少雨な小豆島の気候が塩や大豆、小麦の生産に適し、醤油づくりが根づいたことも、この料理の味付けを支えてきた背景のひとつと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Kakimaze simmers bamboo shoots, green beans, carrot, burdock, dried shiitake, fried tofu, dried shrimp, and fish cake — a mix of ingredients from both sea and mountain — in soy sauce and other seasonings, then mixes them into freshly cooked rice, a dish from Shodoshima also known as "omaze." The broth that each ingredient has absorbed clings lightly to the rice, making for a colorful, festive dish. Shodoshima is known for its soy sauce production, and the local sauce is often what seasons the dish.
## How it's made
Rice is cooked as usual, and dried shiitake and dried shrimp are rehydrated in water. Burdock is shaved into thin strips, green beans are salt-boiled and cut on the diagonal, and the rest of the ingredients are finely chopped. Everything except the carrot and green beans goes into a pot with seasoning and simmers until the flavor soaks in, then the carrot and green beans are added and simmered further. The cooked rice is mixed with the ingredients and their broth, seasoned to taste, and plated. In spring, butterbur or sweet potato stems are sometimes added, and in fishing communities conger eel, giving the dish a seasonal, regional character.
## Why it took this shape
Kakimaze is said to have been served at festive gatherings — family and community events, or times when neighbors helped each other through the busy farming season. Because it comes together quickly and scales easily to feed a crowd, while still looking festive, it's said to have been especially valued by farming women. Shodoshima's mild, dry, sea-surrounded climate suited the production of salt, soybeans, and wheat, which is part of why soy sauce making took root there — and that local sauce, in turn, is part of what shapes the dish's flavor.

sources.title: かきまぜ うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
すしめしの上に酢でしめたサワラを並べ、木箱に詰めて木槌で押し固めた、さぬき市鴨部地域発祥の保存ずし。木枠にくさびを打ち込む際に「カンカン」と音が鳴ることが名前の由来とされる。塩と酢でしっかりとしめたサワラは身が締まって型崩れしにくく、冬なら1週間、夏でも2〜3日ほど保存がきくという。押し固められたすしめしとサワラが一体となった、独特の食感と酸味が持ち味になっている。
## どう作るのか
サワラを刺身にして塩を当て、身の中まで白くなるまで酢でしめる。木箱に葉らんを敷いてすしめしを詰め、その上にサワラを並べて再び葉らんをのせ、蓋をする。いくつもの木箱を重ねて枠に収め、木槌でくさびを打ち込んでしっかりと押し固める。翌日、味がなじんでから切り分けて食べるという。サワラが手に入らない時期は、アジやコノシロで作ることもあるとされる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
讃岐の農家では、麦刈りや田植え前の農閑期にサワラを一本買い、親類を招いてさまざまなサワラ料理を振る舞う「春祝魚」という習わしがあり、カンカンずしもその一つとして作られてきたとされる。木箱に何段も詰めて大量に作れることや、塩と酢でしめて日持ちさせられることから、多くの人手が必要な農繁期を控えた保存食としての役割も果たしてきたと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Kankan-zushi layers vinegar-cured Spanish mackerel over sushi rice packed into a wooden box, then presses it firm with a mallet — a preserved sushi that originated in the Kamobe area of Sanuki city. Its name is said to come from the "kan-kan" sound the mallet makes driving wedges into the wooden frame. Cured thoroughly in salt and vinegar, the mackerel stays firm and holds its shape well, and the sushi is said to keep for about a week in winter and two or three days even in summer. The rice and fish, pressed tightly together, give the dish its distinctive dense texture and tang.
## How it's made
The mackerel is sliced sashimi-style, salted, and cured in vinegar until the flesh turns white all the way through. A wooden box is lined with false lily-of-the-valley leaves, packed with sushi rice, topped with the mackerel, covered with more leaves, and closed with a lid. Multiple boxes are stacked and set into a frame, then wedges are driven in with a mallet to press everything firm. It's left to rest overnight for the flavors to settle before being sliced and served. When mackerel isn't in season, horse mackerel or gizzard shad is sometimes used instead.
## Why it took this shape
Sanuki farming households are said to have had a custom called "haru-iwai-uo," buying a whole Spanish mackerel during the lull before wheat harvest and rice planting to make a variety of mackerel dishes and invite relatives over, and kankan-zushi is said to have been one of those dishes. Being able to pack many boxes at once, and to keep well thanks to the salt and vinegar cure, also gave it a role as a preserved food to have on hand ahead of the labor-intensive farming season.

sources.title: カンカンずし うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
こんにゃくを里芋やにんじん、干ししいたけ、かんぴょうなどとともにだしで煮た、東讃・中讃地域の郷土料理。あっさりとしただしの風味にこんにゃくのぷるんとした食感、里芋のほくほく感が重なり、根菜の甘みが溶け込んだやさしい味わいになる。名前の由来には、味の良さについおかわりを重ねたからとも、こんにゃくを「八杯切り」にするからとも、だしやしょうゆ、酒を合わせて八杯分使うからとも諸説あるという。
## どう作るのか
こんにゃくは3等分してから三角形に薄く切る。干ししいたけは水で戻していちょう切りにし、里芋は食べやすい大きさに切る。かんぴょうは塩でもみ洗いしてから水からゆで、4cmほどに切って結び目を作る。だし汁に干ししいたけの戻し汁を加え、こんにゃくと干ししいたけ、里芋、かんぴょうを煮る。途中でアクを取り除きながら、最後にしょうゆで味を調え、おろししょうがを添えて仕上げる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
こんにゃくは仏教とともに精進料理として伝わったとされ、江戸時代以降に庶民の食材として広まったと伝わる。香川県内では旧琴南町（現まんのう町）や高松市塩江町などでこんにゃく栽培が盛んだったとされ、こうした産地では寒い時季にだしをたっぷり使った煮物として親しまれてきたようだ。かんぴょうや里芋、しいたけなど、当時手に入りやすかった乾物や根菜を組み合わせ、体の温まる料理として定着したと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Konnyaku no hachihai simmers konjac together with taro, carrot, dried shiitake, and kanpyo gourd strips in dashi — a dish from the Higashisanuki and Nakasanuki areas. The light, clean broth meets the springy bite of the konjac and the mealy softness of the taro, with the sweetness of the root vegetables dissolved throughout for a gentle flavor. The name's origin has several accounts: that people found it so tasty they went back for eight helpings, that the konjac is cut into a style called "hachihai-giri," or that the dashi, soy sauce, and sake used add up to eight measures.
## How it's made
The konjac is cut into thirds and then sliced thin into triangles. Dried shiitake is rehydrated and cut into quarter-rounds, and the taro is cut into bite-sized pieces. Kanpyo is rubbed with salt, rinsed, boiled from cold water, cut into four-centimeter lengths, and tied into knots. Dashi is combined with the shiitake's soaking liquid, and the konjac, shiitake, taro, and kanpyo are simmered in it, with any scum skimmed off along the way. It's finished with soy sauce and a garnish of grated ginger.
## Why it took this shape
Konjac is said to have arrived alongside Buddhism as an ingredient for vegetarian temple cooking, spreading to ordinary households from the Edo period on. Konjac cultivation reportedly thrived in areas like the former Kotonami town, now Manno, and Shionoe in Takamatsu, and in those konjac-growing communities the dish seems to have taken root as a hearty, dashi-rich simmer eaten on cold days. Combining dried goods and root vegetables that were readily available at the time appears to be how it settled into a warming winter dish.

sources.title: こんにゃくのはちはい うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
すりつぶした豆腐とごまでこんにゃくをあえた、県内全域に伝わる料理。ごまの香ばしさと豆腐のまろやかな口当たりに、味付けしたこんにゃくのこりこりとした食感が加わり、精進料理らしい素朴で上品な味わいになる。こんにゃくは仏教伝来とともに精進料理として伝わったとも、遣唐使が持ち帰ったとも伝わり、香川県では明治時代からこんにゃく芋の栽培が始まったとされる。そばがらを焼いた灰でアクを作り、生芋から手作りする地域もあるという。
## どう作るのか
豆腐はさっとゆでてざるに上げ、水気を切る。ごまは煎ってすりつぶし、豆腐、みそと合わせてよく練り、砂糖、しょうゆ、塩で味を調える。短冊切りにしたこんにゃくは煎ってから味付けし、最後にすりつぶした豆腐と和えれば完成となる。こんにゃくを先に炒って水分を飛ばしておくことで、味がしみ込みやすくなるという。豆腐はしっかりと水気を切っておくことも、あえ衣をなめらかに仕上げるポイントとされる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
こんにゃくの白あえは、法事や正月など特別な日に作られる料理として広まったとされる。こんにゃくには食物繊維が豊富で腸内環境を整える働きがあるとされ、節分に「一年の砂おろし」として食べる地域が多いという。悪いものを払って新しい年を無病息災で過ごしたいという願いが、節分にこんにゃく料理を食べる習わしに結びついたと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Konnyaku no shiraae dresses konjac in mashed tofu and sesame, a dish found across Kagawa. The nuttiness of the sesame and the mellow texture of the tofu meet the chewy bite of seasoned konjac, giving it the simple, refined character typical of vegetarian temple cooking. Konjac is said to have arrived either alongside Buddhism as part of temple cuisine or to have been brought back by envoys to Tang-dynasty China, and it's said that konjac corm cultivation began in Kagawa in the Meiji era. In some mountain areas it's still made by hand from raw corms, using ash from burned buckwheat husks to remove bitterness.
## How it's made
Tofu is briefly boiled, drained, and pressed to remove excess water. Sesame is roasted and ground, then mixed thoroughly with the tofu and miso, and seasoned with sugar, soy sauce, and salt. Konjac, cut into strips, is pan-roasted and seasoned separately before being tossed with the mashed tofu mixture to finish. Roasting the konjac first to drive off moisture is said to help it take on the seasoning better, and draining the tofu thoroughly is said to be what keeps the dressing smooth.
## Why it took this shape
Konnyaku no shiraae is said to have spread as a dish made for special occasions such as memorial services and New Year's. Konjac is rich in dietary fiber and said to help the gut, and in many areas it's eaten as shiraae or simmered dishes at Setsubun as a way of "clearing out the year," a wish to ward off misfortune and stay healthy through the year ahead. That hope for health and protection appears to be what tied konjac dishes to the Setsubun custom.

sources.title: こんにゃくの白あえ うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
高菜の一種「まんば」を油揚げや豆腐と一緒に炒め煮にした、冬の香川県を代表する家庭料理。まんばは独特のほろ苦さとシャキシャキとした歯ごたえが持ち味で、何度も霜に当たることでやわらかくなり甘みが増すとされる。煮干しの香ばしいだしと豆腐のやさしい味わいが加わり、野菜の少ない冬場でも食べ応えのある一皿になる。細切り野菜と豆腐を炒めるしっぽく料理「けんちん」がなまって「けんちゃん」と呼ばれるようになったと伝わる。
## どう作るのか
まんばはゆでてから水にさらしてアクを抜く。小さめの煮干しは頭ごと、大きいものは頭や内臓、骨を取ってから使う。鍋に油を熱して煮干しを香ばしく炒め、刻んだまんばを加えて炒める。豆腐や油揚げを加えて豆腐を崩しながらさらに炒め、だしや調味料で煮て味を調える。煮干しをしっかり炒って香りを引き出してから野菜を加えるのが、風味を良くするコツとされる。具材や味付けは家庭によってさまざまだという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
まんばは株の外側から葉を摘んでも次々と新芽が出ることから「万葉」と名付けられたと伝わり、県内全域の家庭菜園でも見かける身近な野菜だったとされる。野菜が少なくなる冬場に、庭先で育てやすいまんばを霜に当ててやわらかくし、煮干しや豆腐と炒め煮にすることで栄養を補う料理として根づいたと考えられる。西讃地域では別名「百貫」がなまって「ひゃっか」と呼ばれ、地域によって呼び名が異なるという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Manba no kenchan stir-simmers "manba," a type of mustard green, with fried tofu and tofu — a winter staple across Kagawa. Manba has a distinctive light bitterness and a crisp bite, and repeated exposure to frost is said to soften the leaves and bring out their sweetness. The savory aroma of dried sardine dashi and the gentle taste of tofu round it out, making for a filling dish even in a season with few other vegetables. The name "kenchan" is said to be a slurring of "kenchin," a style of dish that stir-fries shredded vegetables with tofu.
## How it's made
The manba is boiled and then soaked in water to remove its bitterness. Small dried sardines are used whole, heads included, while larger ones have their heads, innards, and bones removed first. Oil is heated in a pan and the sardines are fried until fragrant, then the chopped manba is added and stir-fried. Tofu and fried tofu go in next, the tofu broken up as it cooks, and dashi and seasoning are added to finish. Frying the sardines well before adding the greens is said to be the trick to bringing out their aroma. Both the ingredients and the seasoning are said to vary from household to household.
## Why it took this shape
Manba is said to have gotten its name, meaning "ten thousand leaves," because new shoots keep sprouting even as outer leaves are picked, and it was a familiar vegetable grown in home gardens across the prefecture. In the depths of winter, when few other vegetables were available, growing manba in the yard, letting frost soften it, and stir-simmering it with dried sardines and tofu appears to have become a way of filling out the diet with a nutritious, homegrown ingredient. In western Kagawa it also goes by "hyakka," said to be a slurred form of another old name for the plant.

sources.title: まんばのけんちゃん うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
丸や扇形の木型にすし飯や五目飯を詰めて押し抜いた「物相飯」を指す、三豊市の郷土料理。にんじんやこんにゃく、たけのこ、いりこ、ごぼう、かんぴょう、干ししいたけなどを甘辛く煮た具をご飯に混ぜ込み、型で抜いて成形する。もともとは修行僧が一膳のご飯で食事を済ませる際の精進料理が起源とされ、簡素ながら具材の旨みがしっかり詰まった食べ応えのあるご飯になっている。近年は牛肉を使った「肉もっそ」も見られるという。
## どう作るのか
いりこは頭と腹、骨を取り除いておく。にんじんやこんにゃく、たけのこなどの具材を切り、水と調味料で甘辛く煮る。炊き上がったご飯に具材と煮汁を混ぜ合わせ、円柱形の型に詰めて押し抜き、器に盛り付ければ完成となる。型に押し詰めることで、持ち運びやすく取り分けやすい形に仕上がるといい、押し加減がゆるいと型崩れしやすいため、しっかりと詰めるのがコツとされる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
三豊市では五穀豊穣や海上安全、厄払いを祈願する百々手祭りが毎年開かれてきたとされ、この祭りの会食としてもっそうめしが振る舞われたことから市民に親しまれるようになったと伝わる。祭り以外にも、川ざらえや棟上げなど住民総出の共同作業の際、集まった人にまかないとして振る舞われていたという。型に押し詰めて人数分をまとめて用意できる形が、大勢で作業する機会の多い暮らしに合っていたと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Mossomeshi refers to "busso-meshi," rice pressed into a round or fan-shaped wooden mold — a dish from Mitoyo city. Carrot, konjac, bamboo shoots, iriko, burdock, kanpyo, and dried shiitake, all simmered sweet and savory, are mixed into the rice before it's pressed and shaped in the mold. It's said to have originated as a simple vegetarian meal for monks living communally, meant to be eaten as a single bowl of rice containing everything needed. Despite its simplicity, the dish is packed with the flavor of its many ingredients. A beef version, "niku-mosso," has become common in recent years.
## How it's made
The iriko are headed, gutted, and deboned. Carrot, konjac, bamboo shoots, and the other ingredients are cut and simmered sweet and savory in water and seasoning. Once the rice is cooked, the ingredients and their broth are mixed in, and the rice is packed into a cylindrical mold, pressed out, and plated. Pressing it into a mold is said to give the rice a shape that's easy to carry and easy to portion out for a crowd, and packing it firmly is said to be the key to keeping it from falling apart once unmolded.
## Why it took this shape
Mitoyo is said to hold an annual archery festival called Momote, praying for a good harvest, safety at sea, and protection from misfortune, and mossomeshi is said to have become a local favorite after being served as the communal meal at that festival. Beyond the festival, it was reportedly also served as a working meal whenever residents gathered for shared labor, such as clearing irrigation channels or raising a roof beam. Pressing the rice into a mold so portions for many people could be prepared at once looks well suited to a life with frequent group labor.

sources.title: もっそうめし うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
旬のなすと小豆島特産のそうめんを、唐辛子でぴりっと味を引き締めた家庭料理。油で炒めたなすが煮汁を含んでとろけるような食感になり、そうめんが煮汁を吸ってのど越しよく仕上がる。主食にもおかずにもなるボリュームがあり、食欲の落ちる夏でも食べやすいとされる。香川県西部では、一般的ななすの約3倍の大きさで皮のやわらかい「三豊なす」を使うことも多く、そのとろけるような食感がだしとよく合うという。
## どう作るのか
なすは切り目を入れて水にさらしアクを抜き、水気を取ってから厚手の鍋で油で炒める。油揚げと唐辛子を加え、いりこのだし汁に砂糖としょうゆを加えて煮る。仕上げに、あらかじめ硬めにゆでたそうめんを加えれば完成となる。しょうがやねぎなどの薬味を添えるとさらに風味が増すという。温かくても冷やしても、なすや油揚げに出汁がしみ込んでおいしく食べられるとされる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
そうめんはご飯が足りないときの常備食として重宝され、手早く作れることから主婦の間で広まったと伝わる。なすが油と煮汁を含んでボリュームが出ることから、暑さで食欲が落ちる夏場でも食べやすい一品として定着したと考えられる。小豆島でそうめん作りが盛んだったことと、皮のやわらかい三豊なすが西讃地域で育てられてきたことが結びつき、地域の食材を生かした夏の定番料理になったようだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Nasu somen pairs seasonal eggplant with Shodoshima's famous somen noodles, sharpened with a bit of chili. The eggplant, fried in oil, soaks up the broth into a melting texture, while the noodles absorb the broth for a smooth bite. Hearty enough to serve as a main dish or a side, it's said to be easy to eat even when summer heat dulls the appetite. In western Kagawa, "Mitoyo eggplant" — about three times the size of ordinary eggplant, with thin, tender skin — is often used, its melting texture said to pair especially well with the broth.
## How it's made
The eggplant is scored, soaked in water to remove bitterness, drained, and fried in oil in a heavy pot. Fried tofu and chili are added, followed by dried-sardine dashi, sugar, and soy sauce, and the mixture is simmered. Somen noodles, pre-boiled slightly firm, are stirred in to finish. Ginger or scallion is sometimes added for extra flavor. Served hot or chilled, the eggplant and fried tofu are said to taste good either way once they've soaked up the broth.
## Why it took this shape
Somen is said to have been a handy pantry staple for stretching a meal when there wasn't quite enough rice, and its ease of preparation is said to be why this dish spread widely among households. Eggplant, which turns hearty and filling once it soaks up oil and broth, appears to have become a natural match for a dish meant to be easy to eat in the heat of summer. The pairing of Shodoshima's thriving somen production with the thin-skinned Mitoyo eggplant grown in western Kagawa looks like what turned it into a local summer staple built from ingredients close at hand.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「おちらし」と呼ばれる、はだか麦ともち米を煎って挽いた粉を、水あめと砂糖で練り上げた菓子。「はったい」の別名からも呼ばれる「はったいあめ」と同じもので、香ばしく炒った麦の風味と水あめのねっとりとした甘さが合わさり、噛むほどに香ばしさが広がる。香川では米の裏作としてはだか麦の栽培が昔から盛んで、はだか麦は食物繊維が豊富とされ、味噌や麦茶の材料としても使われてきたという。
## どう作るのか
はだか麦ともち米を10対3の割合で混ぜ、弱火でじっくり煎ってからひき臼で粉にする。鍋に水と水あめ、砂糖を入れて短時間で煮立たせ、そこにおちらし粉を加えて弱火で練り上げる。練り上がったあめをまな板の上で棒状にまとめ、斜めに切り分ける。仕上げに打ち粉用のおちらしをまぶせば、べたつかず食べやすくなるという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
香川は気候が麦の栽培に適しており、米の裏作として古くから麦づくりが行われてきたとされる。麦の収穫期である初夏に合わせ、新しく取れたはだか麦を使って各家庭でおちらしあめを作る習わしが根づいたと考えられる。甘いものが少なかった時代には子どもにも喜ばれ、菖蒲の葉ですくって食べると病気にならないという言い伝えとともに、季節の節目に食べる菓子として親しまれてきたという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Ochirashi-ame is a confection made by roasting and grinding naked barley and glutinous rice into a flour called "ochirashi," then kneading it into a paste of starch syrup and sugar. Also known as "hattai-ame," from another name for the roasted flour, it carries the toasty flavor of the roasted grain alongside the sticky sweetness of the syrup, releasing more aroma with every chew. Kagawa has long grown naked barley as a second crop after rice, thanks to a suitable climate, and the grain, said to be rich in dietary fiber, has also been used to make miso and barley tea.
## How it's made
Naked barley and glutinous rice are mixed in a ten-to-three ratio, roasted slowly over low heat, then ground into flour with a hand mill. Water, starch syrup, and sugar are combined in a pot and briefly brought to a boil, then the ochirashi flour is stirred in and kneaded over low heat. The finished paste is shaped into a stick on a cutting board and sliced on the diagonal. It's finished with a dusting of more ochirashi flour, which is said to keep the pieces from sticking together.
## Why it took this shape
Kagawa's climate suits barley cultivation, and naked barley has long been grown as a second crop after rice is harvested. Making ochirashi-ame from the newly harvested barley around early summer, when the crop comes in, appears to be a custom that took root around that timing in households across the region. In an era when sweets were scarce, it's said to have been especially popular with children, and along with a folk belief that scooping it up with an iris leaf would ward off illness, it seems to have become a treat tied to the turn of the season.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
すし飯とサワラ、そら豆、卵焼きなどの具材を型に詰めて押し出す、四角や扇、松、梅など型に応じた形が楽しめるすし。春から初夏、そら豆に実が入り麦が熟れる頃、脂の乗ったサワラが瀬戸内海に入って旬を迎えるとされる。すし飯の酸味にサワラの脂の甘み、そら豆の淡い風味が重なり、エビやきぬさや、紅しょうがなどの彩りが季節感を演出する一品になっている。
## どう作るのか
型にすし飯を詰め、間に煮た野菜の小切りをはさみ込む。上に山椒とともにサワラ、そら豆、彩りとしてエビや卵焼き、きぬさや、紅しょうがなどを型に並べ、押し出して形を整える。押し型は四角や扇、松、梅などさまざまな形があり、旬の食材を彩りよく盛り込むことで見た目にも華やかに仕上がるという。具材を均等に敷き詰めておくと、押し出したときに断面がきれいに揃うとされる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
讃岐の農家では、麦刈りや田植え前の農閑期にサワラを一本買い、親類を招いてもてなす「春祝魚」という習わしがあったとされ、押し抜きずしはその主役として作られてきたという。若い嫁のいる家では、姑がサワラを持たせて里帰りさせ、実家で作った押し抜きずしを婚家への土産にする風習もあったと伝わり、季節の魚を介して実家と嫁ぎ先の縁をつなぐ役割も果たしていたようだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Oshinuki-zushi packs sushi rice together with Spanish mackerel, fava beans, and rolled egg into a mold and presses it out, taking on whatever shape the mold gives it — square, fan, pine, or plum. From spring into early summer, as fava beans fill out and the wheat ripens, fatty Spanish mackerel is said to move into the Seto Inland Sea and reach its peak season. The tang of the sushi rice meets the richness of the mackerel and the mild flavor of the fava beans, with shrimp, snow peas, and red pickled ginger adding seasonal color.
## How it's made
Sushi rice is packed into a mold, layered with small pieces of simmered vegetables. On top, Spanish mackerel and sansho pepper, fava beans, and colorful garnishes like shrimp, rolled egg, snow peas, and red pickled ginger are arranged in the mold before it's pressed and unmolded. The molds come in various shapes — square, fan, pine, plum — and packing them with colorful seasonal ingredients is said to be what gives the dish its festive look. Spreading the ingredients evenly is said to keep the cross-section neat once it's pressed out.
## Why it took this shape
Sanuki farming households are said to have had a custom called "haru-iwai-uo," buying a whole Spanish mackerel during the lull before wheat harvest and rice planting and inviting relatives over, and oshinuki-zushi is said to have been the centerpiece of that occasion. In households with a young bride, the mother-in-law reportedly sent her home to her parents with a mackerel, and the bride would bring back oshinuki-zushi made there as a gift for her husband's family — a seasonal fish dish that also seems to have served as a way of maintaining ties between the two households.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
焼いた白身魚をほぐし、焦げ目をつけた味噌と魚のだし汁でのばして、熱々のご飯にかける郷土料理。タイのほかチヌやメバル、ボラなど瀬戸内海でとれる白身魚が使われ、香ばしく焼いた味噌の風味と魚の旨みが溶け合った汁がご飯によく絡む。かつては鍋の蓋やすり鉢に味噌を塗り、七輪にかぶせて焼くことで香ばしさを引き出していたという。九州から四国へ海沿いに伝わったとされ、愛媛では「伊予さつま」、香川では「讃岐さつま」とも呼ばれるという。
## どう作るのか
白身魚は塩焼きにしてから骨と皮を除き、身をほぐす。頭と骨は別にだし汁を取っておく。味噌は木杓子につけて軽く焦げ目をつけ、香ばしさを引き出す。すり鉢で魚の身をよくすり、味噌を加えて冷ましただし汁で少しずつのばす。だし汁を熱いまま加えると味噌が分離しやすいため、必ず冷ましてから加えるのがコツとされる。熱々のご飯にかけ、ねぎと軽く煎ってすりつぶしたごまを薬味として添える。
## なぜこの形になったのか
さつまは、魚が多くとれたときの日常食として各家庭の食卓に並んできたとされる。傷みやすい魚を焼いてほぐし、だしまで無駄なく使い切ることで、貴重な米でも満足感を得られるよう工夫された庶民の味として受け継がれてきたと考えられる。香川の特産であるいりこを使うこともあったといい、身近な魚と調味料で作れる手軽さが、各家庭に伝わってきた理由のようだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Satsuma flakes grilled white fish and thins it with charred miso and fish dashi, then pours it over hot rice. Sea bream is common, but black porgy, rockfish, and mullet — other white fish caught in the Seto Inland Sea — are also used, and the smoky flavor of the charred miso melds with the fish's umami into a broth that clings well to the rice. The miso used to be spread on a pot lid or mortar and set over a charcoal brazier to bring out its aroma, it's said. The dish is said to have traveled along the coast from Kyushu to Shikoku, and is also known as "Iyo-zatsuma" in Ehime and "Sanuki-zatsuma" in Kagawa.
## How it's made
The white fish is salt-grilled, then the bones and skin are removed and the meat is flaked. A dashi is made separately from the head and bones. Miso is spread on a wooden spatula and lightly charred to bring out its aroma. The fish is ground well in a mortar, mixed with the charred miso, and thinned gradually with the cooled dashi; adding the dashi while still hot is said to make the miso separate, so it's always cooled first. It's poured over hot rice and topped with scallion and sesame, roasted lightly in a pan and ground for extra fragrance.
## Why it took this shape
Satsuma is said to have become an everyday dish served whenever a household had a good catch of fish. Grilling and flaking fish that spoiled quickly, and using every part down to the dashi, appears to be a way of making the most of it while still getting real satisfaction from precious rice — a humble dish said to have been handed down through households built on that kind of resourcefulness. Iriko, a local specialty, was reportedly sometimes used as well, and the ease of making it from familiar fish and seasonings seems to be why it has been passed down in so many households.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
こんにゃくを主役に、にんじんやごぼう、さつまいも、干ししいたけを合わせただし仕立ての煮物。すりおろしたさつまいもでとろみをつけるため、汁気が多くさらさらと喉を通ることが名前の由来とされる。こんにゃくのこりこりとした食感と、とろみのついた甘みのあるだしが絡み合い、素朴ながら滋味深い味わいになる。よく似た郷土料理に「こんにゃくのはちはい」があるが、こんにゃくの切り方や薬味が異なるという。
## どう作るのか
こんにゃくはさっとゆでて縦に切り、にんじんは千切り、ごぼうはささがきにしてゆでておく。干ししいたけは水で戻して細切りにし、下味をつける。鍋にだし汁と具材を入れ、しょうゆ、砂糖、酒で味付けして煮る。皮をむいてすりおろしたさつまいもを煮立った鍋に加えて混ぜ、とろみがついたら火を止める。器に盛り、刻みねぎとおろししょうがを添えれば完成となる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
三豊市仁尾町の山間部では古くから家の周りにこんにゃく芋を植え、時期になると共同でこんにゃくを作ってアクを入れた樽で保存する習わしがあったとされる。手に入りやすいこんにゃくと根菜を使い、簡単な調理で作れることから、法事や弘法大師の月命日など特別な日の料理として定着したと考えられる。こんにゃくは食物繊維が豊富で腸を整える働きがあるとされ、体をいたわる料理としても重宝されてきたという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Sawasawa centers on konjac, simmered together with carrot, burdock, sweet potato, and dried shiitake in a dashi-based broth. Grated sweet potato thickens the broth, and the watery, easily poured texture that results is said to be the source of the dish's name. The chewy bite of the konjac meets the thickened, faintly sweet broth for a simple but deeply satisfying flavor. A similar dish, "konnyaku no hachihai," exists elsewhere in Kagawa, but differs in how the konjac is cut and in its garnishes.
## How it's made
The konjac is briefly boiled and cut into strips, the carrot julienned, and the burdock shaved into strips and boiled. Dried shiitake is rehydrated, cut into strips, and lightly seasoned. Dashi and the prepared ingredients go into a pot and simmer with soy sauce, sugar, and sake. Peeled, grated sweet potato is stirred into the simmering pot, and once it thickens, the heat is turned off. It's served with a topping of chopped scallion and grated ginger.
## Why it took this shape
In the mountainous part of Toyo in Mitoyo city, households are said to have long grown konjac corms around their homes, making konjac together as a community when the season came and storing dozens of blocks per household in barrels with the bitterness-removing liquid. Made from readily available konjac and root vegetables with a simple method, the dish appears to have become established as a special-occasion food for memorial services and the monthly anniversary of Kobo Daishi's death. Konjac is said to be rich in dietary fiber and to help the gut, which is also said to have made it valued as a dish that's easy on the body.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
瀬戸内海の塩飽諸島に伝わる、茶で炊いたお粥。高知県産の碁石茶やハブ茶、ほうじ茶を煮出した湯で米を炊き上げ、調味料は一切加えない。碁石茶ならではの深い渋みだけが味の決め手で、島の湯水に含まれるわずかな塩気とよく合うとされる。志々島や高見島、佐柳島など田んぼの少ない島々で、貴重な米を少しでも長く食べつなぐための知恵から生まれた一杯だという。
## どう作るのか
釜に湯を沸かして碁石茶やハブ茶、ほうじ茶を煮出し、米を加えて15分から20分ほど煮込めば完成となる。麦や芋、そら豆、正月に残った餅を小さく切って煎ったものを加える家庭もあるといい、使うお茶の配合や具材は家庭ごとに異なるという。味付けをせず茶の風味だけで仕上げるため、しっかりと煮出して茶の渋みを引き出すことが肝心とされ、調理が簡単で手早く食べられることから、漁師にも親しまれてきたという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
志々島をはじめとする塩飽諸島の島々は田んぼがなく、米は魚を売って手に入れる貴重品だったとされる。茶で炊くことでご飯をかさ増しし、少ない米を長く食い延ばす手段として茶粥が定着したと考えられる。かつては丸亀や仁尾の茶商が高知まで茶を買い付けに行っていたと伝わり、遠方から茶を運んでまで作り続けられてきたことが、島の暮らしにとってこの一杯がいかに欠かせなかったかを物語っているようだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Shima no chagayu is a rice porridge cooked in tea, made on the islands of the Shiwaku archipelago in the Seto Inland Sea. Rice is simmered in water brewed with goishi-cha, a fermented tea from Kochi, or with senna or roasted green tea, with no seasoning added at all. The deep astringency of the goishi-cha alone carries the flavor, and it's said to pair especially well with the slightly salty well water found on these islands. On islands like Shishijima, Takamishima, and Sanagishima, with little farmland for rice, the dish is said to have grown out of a need to stretch a precious grain as far as it would go.
## How it's made
Water is boiled in a large pot and brewed with goishi-cha, senna, or roasted green tea, then rice is added and simmered for fifteen to twenty minutes. Some households also add barley, sweet potato, fava beans, or leftover New Year's rice cake, cut small and roasted first. The blend of tea and the added ingredients vary from household to household. Since no seasoning is added at all, brewing the tea strong enough to bring out its full astringency is said to matter most, and because it's quick and simple to make, it's said to have been especially valued by fishermen.
## Why it took this shape
Islands like Shishijima had no rice paddies, and rice reportedly had to be bought with money earned selling fish, making it a precious commodity. Cooking it in tea to stretch the rice and make it last longer appears to be how chagayu became established. Tea merchants from Marugame and Nio are said to have once traveled as far as Kochi to buy the tea, and the effort of carrying it in from so far away suggests just how central this bowl was to life on the islands.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
乾燥させたそら豆を弱火で煎り、熱いうちにしょうゆと砂糖、唐辛子を合わせた調味液に漬け込んだ保存食。煮豆と違って先に豆を煎ってから漬け込むため、軽くかむとホロッとくだける独特の食感が楽しめる。しょうゆの塩気とそら豆の香ばしさ、唐辛子のわずかな辛みが調和し、酒の肴にも常備菜にもなる素朴な味わいとされる。皮ごと食べられるのも特徴で、好みでしょうが汁を加えて風味づけする家庭もあるという。
## どう作るのか
乾燥そら豆をほうろくやフライパンに入れ、弱火でじっくりと煎る。鍋に水、しょうゆ、砂糖を入れて煮立たせた調味液に、煎りたてのそら豆を熱いうちに漬け込み、一晩ねかせる。かつては砂糖をほとんど使わずそら豆本来の甘みを生かしていたが、今は家庭により甘みの加減が異なるという。豆が熱いうちに漬け込むことで調味液がしみ込みやすくなるとされる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
しょうゆ豆は江戸時代の讃岐で生まれたとされ、醤油醸造が始まった小豆島が発祥の地だとする説や、遍路をもてなすために煎っていたそら豆が近くの醤油の壺に転がり込んだことが始まりとする言い伝えもあるという。温暖な気候が育てやすく、稲の裏作としてそら豆が広く栽培されてきたことも、この料理が根づいた背景と考えられる。保存がきくことから、農繁期の常備菜として重宝されてきたとされる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Shoyu mame is a preserved food made by roasting dried fava beans over low heat, then pickling them while still hot in a seasoning liquid of soy sauce, sugar, and chili. Unlike simmered beans, roasting the beans first before pickling gives them a distinctive texture that crumbles cleanly with a light bite. The saltiness of the soy sauce, the toasted flavor of the beans, and a hint of chili heat come together for a simple flavor said to work equally well as a bar snack or a pantry staple. The beans are eaten skin and all, and some households add ginger juice for extra fragrance.
## How it's made
Dried fava beans are roasted slowly over low heat in a special pan or a skillet. A seasoning liquid of water, soy sauce, and sugar is brought to a boil in a pot, and the freshly roasted beans are pickled in it while still hot, then left to rest overnight. In the past, little or no sugar was used, letting the bean's own sweetness carry the flavor, but today the sweetness varies by household. Pickling the beans while hot is said to help the seasoning soak in more easily.
## Why it took this shape
Shoyu mame is said to have originated in Sanuki during the Edo period. One account traces it to Shodoshima, where soy sauce brewing began, and another holds that fava beans being roasted to serve pilgrims rolled into a nearby jar of soy sauce, giving rise to the dish by accident. The mild climate that made fava beans easy to grow as a second crop after rice also appears to be part of why the dish took root here. Because it keeps well, it's said to have been valued as a pantry staple during the busy farming season.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
塩でしめたタイを一匹丸ごと甘辛く煮込み、ゆでたそうめんとともに大皿に盛りつけた、婚礼のごちそうを締めくくる伝統料理。タイの旨みをたっぷり吸ったそうめんと、煮崩れないよう丁寧に煮込まれたタイの身が一体となり、祝いの席にふさわしい華やかな一品になる。詫間町のようにタイを焼いてから盛りつける地域や、ピンクや紫のそうめんを使う地域もあるなど、盛り付け方は土地によってさまざまだという。
## どう作るのか
塩でしめたタイを大鍋に入れ、しょうゆ、砂糖、酒を加えて崩れないよう30分ほど煮込む。大皿にタイを盛り、ゆでたそうめんを流し込めば完成となる。タイを姿焼きにしてからそうめんと盛り付ける地域もあるという。錦糸卵や野菜の飾り切りを添えて彩りよく仕上げることもあるとされ、大皿全体をタイとそうめんで埋め尽くすことが祝い膳らしい豪華さにつながっている。
## なぜこの形になったのか
鯛そうめんは婚礼の宴会で座卓に載せ、讃岐伊勢音頭に合わせて二人がかりで座卓を揺すりながら出す習わしがあったと伝わり、祝いの席を盛り上げる演出の一部として発展してきたと考えられる。棟上げ式や船の進水式でも振る舞われてきたとされ、めでたい席に欠かせない料理として、江戸時代の武家の献立にすでに記録が残るという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Tai somen simmers a whole salt-cured sea bream sweet and savory, then plates it on a large dish together with boiled somen noodles — a traditional dish that caps off a wedding feast. The noodles, soaked in the fish's flavor, and the carefully simmered fish, kept intact without falling apart, come together into a dish festive enough for a celebration. In some areas, such as Takuma, the fish is grilled rather than simmered before plating, and pink or purple-dyed noodles are sometimes used, so the presentation varies by region.
## How it's made
The salt-cured sea bream goes into a large pot with soy sauce, sugar, and sake, and is simmered gently for about thirty minutes so it doesn't fall apart. It's plated on a large dish and topped with boiled somen noodles poured over it. In some areas the fish is grilled whole before being plated with the noodles instead. Shredded egg crepe or decoratively cut vegetables are sometimes added for extra color, and filling the whole platter with fish and noodles is part of what gives the dish its celebratory scale.
## Why it took this shape
At wedding banquets, tai somen is said to have been set on a low table and carried in by two people rocking the table back and forth in time with the Sanuki Ise-ondo song, a piece of theater that appears to have developed as part of the celebration itself. It's also said to have been served at roof-raising ceremonies and boat launchings, and records show that a version of the dish already appeared on samurai household menus in the Edo period, well before it spread more widely as a wedding staple from the Meiji era on.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
発酵が進んで酸味の出た古漬けたくあんを塩抜きし、油で炒めた惣菜。たくあん特有の酸味と歯ごたえに、唐辛子のぴりっとした辛みが加わり、ご飯が進む素朴な味わいになる。冬に大量に漬け込んだたくあんは、春が近づくにつれ発酵が進んで酸っぱくなるため、それを無駄にせず食べきる工夫として生まれたとされる。しょうがの千切りやごまを加えて香りを立たせる家庭もあるという。
## どう作るのか
たくあんを薄い輪切りにし、太いものは半月切りにして1日ほど水にさらし塩抜きする。鍋に塩抜きしたたくあんと水を入れて煮て、一度ざるに上げてから再び水を加えてやわらかくなるまで煮る。水気を切ったたくあんを鍋で炒め、調味料と酒を加えてさらに煮て、最後に輪切りの唐辛子を加えれば完成となる。しっかり塩抜きすることが、食べやすい塩梅に仕上げるコツとされる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
香川では冬に大根を大量に漬け込んでたくあんを仕込む習わしがあったとされ、春に向けて発酵が進み酸味を帯びたたくあんを、塩抜きして油で炒めることで無駄なく食べきる知恵として広まったと考えられる。大根は県内各地で古くから栽培され、味噌汁や煮物、切り干し大根など幅広く食文化を支えてきたとされ、たくあんのきんぴらもその延長線上で生まれた料理といえそうだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Takuan no kinpira is a side dish made by desalting fully fermented takuan pickles and frying them in oil. The pickle's characteristic tartness meets a sharp kick of chili for a simple flavor that goes well with rice. Takuan pickled in large batches over winter grows more sour as fermentation progresses toward spring, and this dish is said to have developed as a way of using up that sourer pickle rather than wasting it. Some households add julienned ginger or sesame for extra fragrance.
## How it's made
The takuan is sliced thin into rounds, or half-moons if the daikon is thick, and soaked in water for about a day to remove the salt. It's simmered in a pot with water, drained, then simmered again with fresh water until tender. Once drained, it's stir-fried in a pan, seasoned with sake and other seasonings, and simmered further, finished with sliced chili. Desalting it thoroughly is said to be the key to getting the balance of flavor right.
## Why it took this shape
Kagawa households are said to have traditionally pickled large batches of daikon into takuan each winter, and frying the increasingly sour pickle in oil after desalting it appears to have become a way of eating it all without waste as spring approached. Daikon has long been grown throughout the prefecture and used in everything from miso soup to dried daikon strips, and takuan no kinpira looks like an extension of that same resourceful use of the vegetable.

sources.title: たくあんのきんぴら うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
讃岐平野のため池にすむフナ（鉄砲）を三枚におろして薄切りにし、塩と酢でしめてから大根とともに白みそベースの酢みそで和えた料理。フナの淡泊な身に酢みその酸味とコクが加わり、細ねぎや唐辛子のアクセントが効いた、酒の肴にもぴったりの一品とされる。冬に水を抜いたため池でとれる「寒ブナ」は脂がのって身が締まり、淡水魚特有の臭みも少ないとされ、てっぱいはその味わいを最も生かせる料理といわれてきたという。
## どう作るのか
フナは三枚におろして細切りにし、塩をかけたあと酢に浸してしめる。大根は短冊切りにして塩もみする。白みそを使った酢みそに刻んだ細ねぎと唐辛子を加え、しめたフナと大根を和えれば完成となる。酢の代わりにだいだいの絞り汁を使ったり、ゆずの皮を千切りにして混ぜたりすることもあり、爽やかな香りを添えるという。フナをしっかり酢でしめることが、淡水魚特有の香りを抑えるコツとされる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
香川は降水量が少なく、農業用水を確保するためのため池が県内各地に数多く作られてきたとされ、そこに生息するフナが身近なたんぱく源になっていたという。農繁期が終わる秋から冬にかけてため池の水を抜く際、産卵を控えたフナが脂ののった食べごろを迎えることから、その時季に合わせて男たちがフナを使った料理を仕込む習わしが根づいたと考えられる。海から遠い山村や農村地域にとって、貴重なたんぱく源を余さず味わう工夫のひとつだったようだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Teppai fillets and thinly slices crucian carp — locally called "teppō" — from the irrigation ponds of the Sanuki plain, cures it in salt and vinegar, and dresses it with daikon in a white-miso vinegar sauce. The mild flavor of the fish meets the tang and richness of the vinegared miso, with scallion and chili adding a sharp accent, making for a dish well suited to a cup of sake. Crucian carp caught in winter, once the ponds are drained, are called "kan-buna," and are said to be especially fatty, firm, and free of the muddy smell sometimes associated with freshwater fish — qualities teppai is said to showcase particularly well.
## How it's made
The crucian carp is filleted and cut into thin strips, salted, and then soaked in vinegar to cure. The daikon is cut into strips and salted. A vinegared white-miso sauce is mixed with chopped scallion and chili, and the cured fish and daikon are tossed in it to finish. Some cooks use the juice of bitter orange in place of vinegar, or mix in julienned yuzu peel, adding a bright citrus aroma to the dish. Curing the carp thoroughly in vinegar is said to be the key to taming its freshwater smell.
## Why it took this shape
Kagawa gets little rainfall, and the prefecture is said to be dotted with irrigation ponds built to secure water for farming, where crucian carp became a familiar source of protein. When the ponds were drained from autumn into winter, once the busy farming season ended, the carp were nearing their spawning period and at their fattiest, and that timing appears to be why men traditionally prepared carp dishes around then. For mountain and farming communities far from the sea, it seems to have been one way of making full use of a valuable source of protein.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
白いうどんに、紅いあん餅やエビ、イクラ、梅干し、かまぼこ、紅しょうがなど赤い食材を添えて食べる、紅白を意識したうどん。太くて長いうどんは古くから長寿を祈る縁起物とされ、そこに赤い彩りを添えることで、新年を祝う華やかな一杯になる。使う赤い食材に決まりはなく、家庭や店ごとにさまざまな組み合わせが楽しまれているという。香川県のさぬきうどん振興協議会が、新たな麺食文化の普及を目的に提案した習慣とされる。
## どう作るのか
白く仕上げたうどんに、梅干しやにんじん、イクラなど好みの赤い食材をトッピングとして添える。紅いあん餅を具材にしたうどんも見られるという。1月15日までに食べることで、その年一年の幸せを願う縁起担ぎとされる。具材の組み合わせに決まりはなく、家庭ごとに自由に工夫できる点が特徴とされ、白いうどんに赤を一色添えるだけで見た目が引き締まるという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
讃岐うどんは、降水量が少なく米作りに向かなかった讃岐地域で、米の代わりとなる麦を使ったうどんが発展してきたと伝わる。良質な小麦といりこが手に入りやすかったことも、うどん文化が根づいた背景と考えられる。太く長いうどんが長寿を願う縁起物とされてきたことに、新年らしい紅白の彩りを重ねることで、うどん文化の土地ならではの新年行事として定着したようだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Toshiake udon dresses white udon noodles with red ingredients — sweet red-bean rice cake, shrimp, salmon roe, umeboshi, fish cake, or red pickled ginger — in a nod to the red-and-white color scheme of celebration. Thick, long udon noodles have long been considered a lucky food associated with long life, and adding a touch of red turns the noodles into a festive bowl for greeting the new year. There's no fixed set of red ingredients, so the combination varies from household to household and shop to shop. The custom is said to have been proposed by the Sanuki Udon Promotion Council as a way of encouraging a new noodle-eating tradition.
## How it's made
Plain white udon is topped with whatever red ingredients are on hand — umeboshi, carrot, salmon roe, and so on. Some versions include red bean-paste rice cake as an ingredient in the noodles themselves. Eating it by January 15 is said to carry a wish for happiness through the coming year. With no fixed combination of toppings, part of the appeal is said to be the freedom each household has to put its own spin on it, since even a single touch of red is enough to set off the white noodles.
## Why it took this shape
Sanuki udon is said to have developed in a region with little rainfall that was poorly suited to rice farming, where wheat noodles took the place of rice as a staple. Access to good-quality wheat and iriko is also said to have been part of why the local noodle culture flourished. Layering the season's red-and-white color scheme onto udon, already valued as a lucky food for its thick, long shape, appears to be what turned it into a New Year's custom distinct to this noodle-loving region.

sources.title: 年明けうどん うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
いりこだしに大根やにんじん、里芋などの季節の野菜をふんだんに入れ、塩を使わず小麦粉と水だけでこねた手打ちめんをそのまま加えて煮込んだ汁物。めんの太さが均一でないのも手作りならではの味わいで、いりこの旨みと野菜の甘みが溶け込んだ汁にめんがもちもちとした食感を添える。打ち立てのめんを別ゆでせずそのまま鍋に打ち込むことから「打ち込み汁」と呼ばれるようになったとされる。
## どう作るのか
ボウルに小麦粉と水を入れて簡単にこね、生地をねかせておく。その間に大根やにんじんなどの具材を切り、鍋にだしを入れて具材を煮る。生地をのばして切っためんを、煮汁が沸騰したところへそのまま加え、めんが煮えたらみそで味を調えて仕上げる。最後にねぎを添えるという。鶏肉や豚肉、しいたけなどを加える家庭もあり、しょうゆで味を調える場合もあるとされる。
## なぜこの形になったのか
温暖で雨の少ない香川は小麦の生産に適しており、小麦粉が家庭で身近な食材として使われてきたとされる。手打ちうどんがハレの日のごちそうだったのに対し、打ち込み汁は農村の冬の寒い日に手早く作れる日常食として広まったと考えられる。めんをゆでこぼさずそのまま汁に加えることで洗い物や手間を減らせる点も、忙しい農作業の合間に重宝された理由のひとつと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Uchikomi-jiru is a soup made by loading dried-sardine dashi with seasonal vegetables like daikon, carrot, and taro, then adding hand-pulled noodles made from nothing but wheat flour and water, no salt, straight into the pot. The noodles' uneven thickness is part of the charm of making them by hand, and their chewy bite meets a broth rich with the flavor of the sardines and the sweetness of the vegetables. Dropping the freshly rolled noodles straight into the pot without boiling them separately first is said to be why it's called "uchikomi-jiru," meaning roughly "pounded-in soup."
## How it's made
Wheat flour and water are kneaded together simply in a bowl and left to rest. While the dough rests, daikon, carrot, and other vegetables are cut and simmered in dashi in a pot. The rested dough is rolled out and cut into noodles, which go straight into the boiling broth; once cooked, the soup is seasoned with miso to finish, with scallion added on top. Some households add chicken, pork, or shiitake, and some season with soy sauce instead of miso.
## Why it took this shape
Kagawa's mild, dry climate suits wheat cultivation, and wheat flour has long been a familiar staple in local kitchens. Where hand-pulled udon was reserved for festive occasions, uchikomi-jiru appears to have spread as an everyday dish farming households could put together quickly on a cold winter day. Adding the noodles straight into the broth without boiling them separately also cut down on extra pots and effort, which looks like part of why it suited a busy life built around farm work.

sources.title: 打ち込み汁 うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
こしあんを餅で渦巻き状に巻いた、引田地域の郷土菓子。渦は鳴門の海を表しているとされ、もちもちとした餅生地の中からこしあんの上品な甘さがのぞく、見た目にも印象的な菓子になっている。かつて鳴門は引田地域にとって大切な漁場だったが、争いに敗れてその海を失った名残を惜しんで作られたのが始まりと伝わる。切り分けた断面に現れる渦模様も、この菓子ならではの見どころとされる。
## どう作るのか
こしあんに小麦粉を加えてよく混ぜ、強火で蒸す。だんご粉はぬるま湯でこねてひとまとめにし、同様に蒸す。蒸し上がったこしあんを粘りが出るまでよくこね、めん棒で厚さ1cmほどの長方形にのばす。だんごも冷めないうちに同じ大きさの長方形にのばし、こしあんと重ねて両手で押さえながらはみ出さないよう丁寧に巻いていく。直径7〜8cmほどになるまで巻いたら、食べやすい長さに切り分ける。
## なぜこの形になったのか
海運交易で栄えた引田地域では、女の子が生まれると初節句に豪華なひな飾りを設ける「引田飾り」という風習があり、子孫繁栄を願うわけぎやハマグリとともに、うずまきもちも菱餅などと並べて飾り、子どもの健やかな成長を願って食べられてきたとされる。海とともに生きてきた地域だからこそ、失われた海への思いを渦の形に込め、子どもの成長を願う行事の菓子として受け継がれてきたと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Uzumaki-mochi wraps smooth red bean paste in a spiral of mochi dough, a confection from the Hiketa area. The spiral is said to represent the sea off Naruto, and the visual is striking — the chewy dough giving way to reveal the refined sweetness of the bean paste inside. Naruto was once said to be an important fishing ground for the people of Hiketa, and the sweet is said to have first been made as a way of honoring that lost sea after Hiketa lost a dispute over it. The swirl revealed in each sliced piece is said to be the confection's signature detail.
## How it's made
Wheat flour is mixed thoroughly into smooth bean paste, which is then steamed over high heat. Separately, dango flour is kneaded with lukewarm water into a single mass and steamed the same way. The steamed bean paste is kneaded until it turns elastic, then rolled out with a rolling pin into a rectangle about a centimeter thick. The dango dough, while still warm, is rolled into a matching rectangle, layered with the bean paste, and rolled up carefully by hand so neither the paste nor the dough spills out, until the roll is seven or eight centimeters across. It's then sliced into manageable lengths.
## Why it took this shape
Hiketa, which prospered through maritime trade, is said to have had a custom called "Hiketa kazari," in which a family with a newborn daughter set up an elaborate display of hina dolls for her first Girls' Festival to show off to the neighborhood. Uzumaki-mochi, alongside lucky items like green onion and clams meant to wish for descendants, was displayed and eaten together with diamond-shaped rice cakes as part of that wish for a child's healthy growth. In a community shaped by the sea, folding the memory of a lost fishing ground into a spiral shape, and tying it to a wish for a child's future, appears to be what carried this confection forward through the town's biggest family celebration.

sources.title: うずまきもち うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
ゆでたわけぎとゆでたタコを、酢でのばした白みそで和えた料理。わけぎはねぎとたまねぎの雑種とされ、ねぎよりも香りがやわらかく、加熱すると甘みが増す。白みその甘みと酢のまろやかな酸味が、わけぎのやさしい香りとタコの弾力ある歯ごたえに絡み、春らしいさっぱりとした味わいになる。地域によってはタコの代わりに、同じく春に旬を迎えるマテ貝やアサリを使うこともあるという。
## どう作るのか
わけぎは白い根元と青い部分に分け、それぞれ3cmほどに切る。沸騰した湯にまず根元を入れ、続けて青い部分をゆでてざるに上げて冷ます。タコは塩もみしてから熱湯でさっとゆで、一口大に切る。すり鉢に白みそ、練りからし、酢、砂糖を入れてよくすり混ぜ、冷ましてからわけぎとタコを和えれば完成となる。かつては年末に雑煮用に作った白みそを残しておき、これに使う家庭もあったという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
わけぎは球根から芽が伸びて枝分かれしながら育つことから、子孫繁栄の縁起物とされ、ひな祭りの時期に食べられてきたと伝わる。小豆郡の豊島では、わけぎを切らずに一口大に巻いて使う「わけぎのぐるぐる」という風習があるといい、良いことが続くようにとの願いが込められているという。山の食材であるわけぎと海の食材であるタコを組み合わせることで、春に恵まれる山海両方の幸を一皿にまとめた料理になったと考えられる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Wakegiae dresses boiled wakegi (a scallion relative) and boiled octopus in white miso thinned with vinegar. Wakegi is said to be a cross between scallion and onion, milder in aroma than ordinary scallion and sweeter once cooked. The sweetness of the white miso and the mellow tang of the vinegar wrap around the wakegi's gentle fragrance and the octopus's springy bite for a refreshing, spring-appropriate flavor. In some areas razor clams or Manila clams, also in season in spring, are used in place of octopus.
## How it's made
The wakegi is separated into its white base and green top, each cut into roughly three-centimeter lengths. The white parts go into boiling water first, followed by the green parts, then both are drained and cooled. The octopus is rubbed with salt, briefly boiled, and cut into bite-sized pieces. White miso, hot mustard, vinegar, and sugar are ground together well in a mortar, and once cooled, the wakegi and octopus are tossed in it. Some households used to save leftover white miso from making New Year's zōni to use in this dish.
## Why it took this shape
Wakegi grows by sending up shoots from a bulb that branch off into more shoots, and it's said to have become a symbol of family prosperity eaten around the Doll Festival for that reason. On Teshima island in Shozu county, there's reportedly a custom called "wakegi no guruguru," in which the wakegi is rolled into bite-sized bundles rather than cut, a wish for good things to keep on coming. Pairing wakegi, a mountain vegetable, with octopus from the sea appears to be a way this dish brought together the best of both, in season together each spring.

sources.title: わけぎあえ うちの郷土料理

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
長方形の木箱を斜めに二つ割りにした「わりご」と呼ばれる器に、型抜きしたご飯と具だくさんの煮しめを詰め合わせたお弁当。こんにゃくやしいたけ、にんじん、ごぼう、ちくわ、れんこんなどを少し濃いめに味付けし、卵焼きやかまぼこなどで彩りよく仕上げる。2個で1人前とされ、20人前40個を負い紐のついた木箱にまとめて持ち運ぶのが習わしだったという。小豆島に古くから伝わる独自の幕の内弁当とされる。
## どう作るのか
専用の木枠でご飯を型抜きし、わりごに詰める。こんにゃく、しいたけ、にんじん、ごぼう、ちくわ、れんこんなどを煮しめにし、れんこんやごぼう、こんにゃくはやや濃いめに味をつけて彩りよく詰め合わせる。卵焼きやかまぼこなども添え、彩り豊かに仕上げるのが特徴とされる。煮しめの具材や味付けは家庭ごとに異なるため、持ち寄るとさまざまな味を楽しめるという。
## なぜこの形になったのか
小豆島では毎年5月3日、農業用ため池の完成を祝って始まったと伝わる「肥土山農村歌舞伎」が開催され、その演目の合間にわりご弁当が食べられてきたとされる。歌舞伎見物のように長時間人が集まる行事で、大人数分をまとめて持ち運べる木箱の形が定着したと考えられる。各家庭で作った弁当を持ち寄り分け合う習わしが、多様な味を楽しむ機会にもなってきたようだ。

## What it's made of
Warigo bento packs mold-shaped rice and a hearty assortment of simmered vegetables into "warigo," rectangular wooden boxes split diagonally in two. Konjac, shiitake, carrot, burdock, fish cake, and lotus root are simmered with a slightly bolder seasoning, and rolled egg or fish cake add color. Two boxes are said to make one portion, and forty boxes for twenty people were traditionally packed into a black lacquered case with a carrying strap. It's said to be a distinctive style of bento long associated with Shodoshima.
## How it's made
Rice is shaped using a dedicated wooden mold and packed into the warigo box. Konjac, shiitake, carrot, burdock, fish cake, and lotus root are simmered together, with the lotus root, burdock, and konjac seasoned a bit more strongly, then packed in colorfully. Rolled egg and fish cake round out the presentation. Since the ingredients and seasoning of the simmered vegetables vary by household, bringing several boxes together lets everyone sample a range of flavors.
## Why it took this shape
Shodoshima holds an annual rural kabuki performance on May 3, said to have begun as a celebration of the completion of an agricultural irrigation pond, and warigo bento is said to have been eaten during breaks in the performance. In a gathering that kept people together for hours watching kabuki, a wooden box built to carry a large batch of portions for many people at once appears to be what settled into this shape. The custom of each household bringing its own box to share also seems to have turned the meal into a chance to sample everyone's own version.
